paragraphs.text: Native macOS frosted glass for the DeepSeek Harness Desktop window
# dsh-frosted-glass
**English** | 中文

Native macOS frosted glass for the DeepSeek Harness Desktop window —
the UI's panes show the window'
s real vibrancy material instead of painting over it.
## What it does

The Desktop shell already asks macOS for a native material and a transparent window
(`vibrancy: "sid

ebar"`, `backgroundColor: "#00000000"`). The Web GUI then paints every pane opaque,
so the material
never shows. This plugin re-tints those panes with an alpha color:
- the window reads as one piece of frosted glass, and the blur stays **native** — macOS composites i

ge-style surfaces lose the sticky header strip that turned one step darker than the body once the
ti
nt became translucent.
## Requirements

| Host | DSH Desktop **on macOS** (`dsh >= 0.2.0-rc.1`) |
| Not supported | the Web GUI in a browser
tab — there is no window material to show through |
It also honours the system **Reduce transparency** setting and macOS full-screen mode by falling bac

k
to solid surfaces, the way native apps do.
## Install
From the plugin page (**插件 → 添加插件**), install it by spec:

- npm: `dsh-frosted-glass`
- a checkout: `file:/absolute/path/to/dsh-frosted-glass`
Then toggle **frosted-glass** on. The page reloads the module; no app restart is needed.
To remove it, toggle the bundle off or remove it from the plugin page.
## Tuning
The plugin ships two knobs, both in the stylesheet at the top of `lib/client.js` — the percentage is
opacity, so a lower number is more transparent:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The sidebar has its own alpha, since macOS already mixes the sidebar fill with 50% transparency:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Edit the file, then toggle the plugin off and on to reload it.
## How it works

A bundle can ship both a host half and a browser half, so this one package is enough:
`dsh.bundle` p

oints at `cordis.patch.yml` (which adds one Loader row) and `dsh.client` points at the
browser bundl
e. The browser half appends one `<style>` element when the module materializes.
Everything is selector-driven, never a patched app binary:
- `--dsw-alias-bg-base` is the token every pane paints, so tinting that one variable makes the windo

t paint the same token again (conversation root, page roots, tab hosts) are set
transparent, so ever
y main surface keeps exactly one tint layer.
## Limitations

- macOS Desktop only; Windows and the browser get no visual change.
- The selectors use CSS-module *

*local names** (`pageBar`, `pageBody`, `TabHost`, the conversation's
column-width custom property),

not hashed class names, so they survive rebuilds — but a major layout
refactor can still break them.
- macOS "Reduce transparency" and full screen win over the plugin by design.
